data.translation: Wir gingen in die Dörfer zum Verzinken. <...>

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Bilgic Der Beruf eines Kesselverzinkers/4)

data.turoyo: Əzzanwo laq qəryawoṯo bu byoḏ̣o, mbayḏ̣inawo səfoqe.
data.translation: Wir gingen in die Dörfer zum Verzinken. Wir verzinkten (Metall-) Gefäße.

rationale: First active Infectum-wa box; complete village-work context with explicit vessel object.

summary: New box Nomen Actionis: example for sense 1 in Nomen Actionis (JTM 1.5/6)

data.turoyo: W uno, u Yaḥqub, u abro du Sleman mbayḏ̣ono, i naqqayo naʕimo wi qəm ide du babi, samnowo i ṣənʕa d babi, byeḏ̣a. <...>
data.translation: Und ich, Yaḥqūb, der Sohn von Sleman dem Verzinner, war damals noch klein, ich ging meinem Vater zur Hand und praktizierte das Handwerk meines Vaters, das Verzinnen. <...>

rationale: First Nomen Actionis example; craft noun byeḏ̣a in explicit apposition, kept separate from byoḏ̣o Infinitiv.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JTM 1.5/9)

data.turoyo: Ba trani w bi quwe du kətono, mibayaḏ̣wo u səfoqo, məd mu laǧan, lu dasto, lu ṣaḥno du muklo, li angariye, li tapske, lu mansaf la sfoqe du muklo kulle, hul li čamčke, lu čanaq, li maġrafto, hul li mqašše <...>
data.translation: Mit diesen beiden, und mit der Wirkung der Baumwolle, wurde das Geschirr verzinnt, vom lăgan (Bottich) bis zum dasto (Kessel), zum Essteller, zur angăriye (flachen Schüssel), zur tapske (kleine Servierplatte), zum mansaf (Servierplatte), (kurz) zum gesamten Essgeschirr, bis hin zur čamčke (Schöpflöffel), dem čanaq (Schöpfkelle), der maġrafto (große Schöpfkelle), und der mqašše (Schaumlöffel). <...>

rationale: First Detransitive Infectum-wa box; means marked with b- and no expressed agent.

summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.5/12)

data.turoyo: U ǧloyo i maʕnayḏe, u səfoqo d əṯewo, manḍafwole mu ʕaǧaq, mu wasax d lə foyəš aʕle, w nufaqwo u ṣəfərayḏe d lo wasax d foyəš, lašan d mosək darmono w d mibayəḏ̣.
data.translation: Waschen bedeutet ... wenn ein Stück Geschirr ankam, reinigte man es von dem Dreck, von dem Schmutz, damit er nicht daran haften blieb, damit sein Kupfer zum Vorschein kam und ohne Schmutz war, damit es das Mittel annahm und sich verzinnen ließ.

rationale: First Detransitive Infectum box; cleaning and chemical adhesion supply the context for d mibayəḏ̣. Retain the edition's complete sentence rather than invent antecedents.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Hanna Dewo/185)

data.turoyo: I. As+sefoqe bməqqa kalla mbayḏútuwanne? Yani, u+kalla bu+waxtawo, bmə́qqawa u+kilo?
data.translation: The utensils, for how much money did you repair them? Like, the money at that time, how much was one kilo?

rationale: Sparse new Infectum-wa cell; second-person plural and object suffix in a price question.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Hanna Dewo/186)

data.turoyo: <...> Ínaqqa, ínaqqa d ʔaḥna … maṭino las+sefoqe, mbayḏíwayna u+kilaṯṯe bəšti+qurùš. <...>
data.translation: <...> When, when we … I got to utensils, we would repair them for 60 kuruş a kilo. <...>

rationale: Fifth active Infectum-wa example; plural craft agents with rate per kilo.

summary: New box Part act.: example for sense 1 in Part act. (MAC Hanna Dewo/214)

data.turoyo: ḤD. E, maǧbúr! Ḥa+mbayḏono, ŭ ḥa+ǧaloyo ŭ ḥa+nafoḥo.
data.translation: Yes, it’s necessary! One tinsmith, one polisher, and one blower.

rationale: First Part act. box; occupational mbayḏono is treated in parallel with the permitted nfḥ lookup's nafoḥo example.

summary: New box Part act.: example for sense 1 in Part act. (Jan 3.49/1322)

data.turoyo: Baṯ-qiyomo Maḥbe: Haymən babi mbayḏ̣ono wa. Mbayḏ̣ono wa, əzzawalle laq qəryawoṯe w ʕammi ste hawxa.
data.translation: Widow Mahbe: Believe me, my father was a tinner. He was a tinner; they used to go to the villages, and my uncle too, like that.

rationale: Thin Part act. cell already exists in round 1; a named father with past copula corroborates the occupational derivative. The repeated token is not duplicated. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (Jan 3.49/1338)

data.turoyo: Ǧan: Ya mama, naqqat əzzənwo hawxa lu bəyoḏ̣o, amṭanwo zad aʕmayye. Koṯe l boləx, mən zad amṭanwo aʕmayye mi Bšeriye ya m ġer qəryawoṯo?
data.translation: Jan: Mother, when they used to go like that for tinning, they would bring provisions with them. Do you remember what provisions they would bring with them from Bisheriye or from other villages?

rationale: Thin round-1 Infinitiv cell gains an explicit purpose of itinerant craft travel. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (Jan 3.49/1340)

data.turoyo: Faqaṭ bu beyoḏ̣o mbayḏ̣iwo as sefoqe du ʕamo, maydiwo lu kallaṯṯe.
data.translation: But in tinning, they used to tin the people's utensils; they used to take their money.

rationale: Thin Infinitiv cell gains beyoḏ̣o as a work-domain expression alongside an overt active vessel theme. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC Hanna Dewo/192)

data.turoyo: <...> ‘Lə+gəmbayḏutu as+sefoqaṯxu?’ ‘Bele! Haymén gəmbayḏínanne!’ Oṯíwayna ləḥḏoḏe. ‘U+kilo bmən? Bməqqa gəmbayḏútulan?’ <...>
data.translation: <...> ‘Won’t you repair your utensils?’‘Sure! I swear we shall repair them!’ We would come to an agreement (lit. ‘we would come to each other’). ‘How much is a kilo (lit. ‘the kilo is at what [price]’)? For how much will you repair it for us?’ <...>

rationale: Client-subject extension and beneficiary -lan in one short exchange; no additional sense or stem required.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 80/73)

data.turoyo: U qaṭuno omər: "Kazzino mbayaḏ̣no as səfoqe di qriṯaṯi." <...>
data.translation: "Ich gehe in diesem Dorfe die Geschirre verzinnen", antwortete er. <...>

rationale: Sparse literal Infectum cell; unprefixed first-person form with explicit village vessels.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 80/84)

data.turoyo: Əmmi: "Mə ṣənʕa kit b iḏayxu?" Əmmi: "Kəmbayḏ̣ina."
data.translation: Da fragten die Leute: "Was für ein Handwerk treibt ihr?" "Wir sind Kesselflicker", antworteten sie.

rationale: Brings literal Infectum cell to five; craft is elicited directly, while the edition's Kesselflicker is not substituted with a new translation.

summary: Literal II.1 now has Preterit and forms with -wa in both agent-coded and Infectum patterns. MAC m̩bā́ḏwayli contrasts with m̩bā́ḏwayno; preserve accents, syllabic marking and ḏ beside the glossary's ḏ̣.
JTM 1.5/9 and /12 show process-oriented Detransitive clauses with vessels as subjects, chemical/cotton means and no agent; inherited 112/83 remains the result-state Part. Pass. whitewashing example.
byoḏ̣o is provisionally filed as Infinitiv; byeḏ̣a is the craft Nomen Actionis. These nominal uses do not establish free interchangeability or a complete productive paradigm.
Occupational mbayḏono is included under Part act. in line with the glossary_lookup.py entry nfḥ treatment of occupational nafoḥo. No sense of merely being a craftsman is added to the numbered list.
MAC translations often say mend/repair where the technical context specifies tinning. The English is retained as supplied, not used to create a general repair sense.
The face/honour construction is already sense 2, including šaraf, so it is not duplicated in Idiomatic phrases. No new idiom is claimed.
Jan adds no numbered sense or box after round 1. The technical craft remains II.1, and no face/honour II.2 token occurs.
Source byḏ forms without the dot below ḏ coexist with byḏ̣. Copy each spelling exactly; the supplied root assignment is supported by the vessel/copper/tinning context.
Round 1 already supplies Part act., Infinitiv, Infectum-wa and a numbered Detransitive sense. Reader missing-box observations are superseded by that baseline.

mi- at Jan 3.49/1328 may mark Detransitive, contrasting with active mbayḏ̣iwa earlier in the same paragraph. The supplied English renders both actively, so it is unsuitable for illustrating the voice distinction and is not quoted as a Detransitive example.
Are byoḏ̣o and byeḏ̣a productive Infinitiv versus lexical craft noun, or should both ultimately be Nomen Actionis? The present filing distinguishes their source distribution.
Confirm occupational mbayḏono as Part act. for this entry, following nfḥ, rather than treating it solely as a lexical profession noun.
Confirm customer-as-subject service causation at MAC Hanna Dewo/192; the Turoyo dialogue supports the role shift, while the English leaves the craftsmen implicit.
At MAC Hanna Dewo/243, is mbayḏən an abandoned craft verb, intended bleaching/washing, or another restart? It supplies no published new sense.
Verify prs 234/26 against PrS 80/86 before modifying the inherited citation.
At MAC Hanna Dewo/188, does hən introduce an abandoned construction before first-person mbayḏíwayna?

Jan 3.49/1328: is mibayḏ̣iwa Detransitive or an epenthetic active variant? The project machine translation gives active “they would tin them” for both clauses; verify the voice and translation before adding this example.
Confirm whether occupational mbayḏ̣ono belongs under Part act. or a lexical profession noun, as already queried in round 1.
Confirm the productive Infinitiv versus craft Nomen Actionis distinction for bəyoḏ̣o/beyoḏ̣o; Jan corroborates the round-1 nominal series without establishing interchangeability.
Restore missing i in deinem Vater
rationale: The possessive before Vater must be deinem. The supplied edition translation repeats denem, but that is itself an evident German typo; it is not a wording preference.

summary: Customers are addressed as subjects of tinning, while craftsmen are understood; the following question explicitly marks the customers as beneficiaries with -lan.
The owner/population can be subject of tinning while craftsmen do the work, corroborating the round-1 client-subject service interpretation. Do not infer a new stem or a general repair meaning.
Possible mibayḏ̣iwa process clause corroborates the round-1 Detransitive proposal, with utensils as subject and no agent; the active alternative remains unresolved.
